title: RVLRY: Recess beyond colour and type
summary: Compare three interactive treatments with rotation, shadows, stickers and irregular paper shapes. The app is unchanged.
body:
Three isolated Recess mockups explore how much physical character to add. These are proposals; none has been incorporated into the app.

Open JNAS → Media → DropBox → RVLRY-recess-materials → index.html, or extract RVLRY-recess-materials.zip and open index.html. The entire folder works offline. Kestrel collects your feedback; interactive mockups open separately.

| Direction | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| A · Sticker Stack | Restrained rotation, layered stickers and crisp offset shadows. |
| B · Cut-Paper Playground | More expressive, irregular rounded paper surfaces and dimensional controls. |
| C · Craft-Table Collage | The boldest torn/scissor-cut silhouettes and assembled collage details. |

Compare the same picker, handoff, play and results screens. Try Correct, Skip, returning skipped words, Hint and Pause to feel the press states. Sample data is illustrative; no game progress is saved. Text, timers and action controls stay level during play, with decoration concentrated in their backing shapes.

My starting recommendation is B for menus and handoffs, with the quieter treatment during play. You can also mix individual details. Similar material treatments could later give Pub Trivia ticket edges, Margin Note folded paper/highlighter details, and Observatory engraved corners and metallic layers. Those other theme changes are not included in this implementation.

Answers are stored in Kestrel and reviewed when this work resumes; submitting does not automatically start an agent or update the app.

questions.label: Which shapes, rotations, shadows or press effects should we keep or change? Should menus be more expressive than active play?
